Why I made this

A brand with a real story, and a season coming fast.

Thank you for connecting with me. I am Mongolian, I finished my MBA in Vancouver this year, and my background is marketing and analytics in fintech.

Many stores in Vancouver sell cashmere from Mongolia. GERDENE is different: it was founded by someone who grew up in Mongolia, so the story of the steppe, the herders and the craft is truly your own. I put together one idea for this holiday season that puts that story front and centre, with a simple way to measure if it works. Everything here is a starting point for you to shape.

The idea

12 Days of GERDENE.

A digital advent calendar, December 1 to 12. It ends early on purpose, so gifts bought on the last day still arrive before Christmas. Nothing new to manufacture: it uses products you already have.

One product

A different piece each day, moving from small gifts to the hero pieces when gift buying peaks.

One story

A short post or reel on the heritage behind it: the herders, the steppe, the craft.

One reason today

A small 24 hour reason to buy, without big discounts that cheapen the brand.

Open a door
0 of 12 opened

A sample lineup from your current range and prices. You choose the final twelve.

The twist

Collect three, unlock the finale.

Customers who buy any 3 products from the 12 Days unlock a reward. It keeps people coming back to see the next door, and it shows us how many customers buy more than once.

123✦

Your choice of reward. Pick one to see it:

20% off the Day 12 piece

Pushes the premium finale when gift buying peaks.

10% store credit on their total

Brings them back in January, usually a quiet month for retail.

A small cashmere accessory as a gift

Uses stock you already have and feels generous.

Content plan

Simple shoots, from the steppe to Vancouver.

Two kinds of content, both ready before December 1. The Mongolia steps use photos and video you already have, like the landscape footage on your website, or clips from your suppliers. The product steps are simple new shoots in the store: a phone, good light and the pieces themselves. I plan the stories and shot list for every day.

01

The steppe

Herding families raise cashmere goats on the open steppe, as they have for generations.

02

Spring combing

Each spring the soft undercoat is combed, not sheared, by herders you work with directly.

03

Natural fibre

Most pieces are left undyed and untreated, with no harsh chemicals.

04

Made in Mongolia

Every step, from combing to knitting, happens in Mongolia.

05

Vancouver and Calgary

In your stores and online, ready for Canadian winters.

06

Your customer

Worn, gifted and kept for years.

Swipe to follow the journey → Steps 01 to 04 use your existing Mongolia footage. Steps 05 and 06 are shot in store.
